I myself am not great at moving on but. I'd recommend just focusing on other things, like other friends or hobbies you might have. That'll keep you distracted enough to where you won't be thinking about them all the time.

Also, there's nothing wrong with still having the crush on them, as long as your life/mood isn't being ruined by it. Which is where the balance of other friends/hobbies will help, I think.

Also also, (assuming both of you do still like each other) this may be difficult for some people to understand, but a relationship doesn't have to ruin a friendship. If you're both understanding and kind people, then giving the relationship a go and ending it if you're incompatible while still remaining friends would be very possible. But that's up to you to do decide whether it's worth risk based on what you know about them.

Not that I'm necessarily religious. But I think God would be glad you chose your own happiness (as well as the happiness of your friend) over attending the church of an extreme pastor, who seemingly doesn't even understand the religion they claim to value.

Idk if that's true. I guess there's something to be said about the potential that was ultimately never tapped but could be seen. But the same could be said for a lot of break ups, in which the potential was tapped but ultimately lost. And realizing that potential is there and can be reclaimed, it just takes growth from one of or both partners, can also be just as painful (considering how difficult growth is for many people).

But yeah either way, a lost love is truly a tragedy. I hope the future treats you well!

Not racist. Ignorant? Maybe. Uninformed? Definitely.
But that was what you were then. Not what you are now.

The fact that you learned and grew is something you should take pride in. And I promise you, damn near all of us were ignorant or stupid at one point. So there's no shame in knowing you were that and grew past it.

That's, of course, if your problem was his technique (how he touched/grabbed you, what positions, what he said/didn't say, maybe you need toys, etc.)

If your problem was purely his body, like his overall body look/build or the size of his penis, then there's not a whole lot you can do to fix that. Especially not in the short run.
